# <img src="framework-docs/src/docs/spring-framework.png" width="80" height="80"> Spring Framework [![Build Status](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/actions/workflows/build-and-deploy-snapshot.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/actions/workflows/build-and-deploy-snapshot.yml?query=branch%3Amain) [![Revved up by Develocity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Revved%20up%20by-Develocity-06A0CE?logo=Gradle&labelColor=02303A)](https://ge.spring.io/scans?search.rootProjectNames=spring)

> Java開発者向けに、DI・AOP・MVC・データアクセスなど幅広い基盤機能をモジュール構成で提供するエンタープライズアプリケーションフレームワーク。

## Guide

- [All Modules](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/src/docs/api/dokka-overview.md): _See also the <a href="../javadoc-api/" target="_blank">Java API documentation (Javadoc)</a>._
- [Spring Framework - Eclipse/STS Project Import Guide](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/import-into-eclipse.md): This document will guide you through the process of importing the Spring Framework projects into Eclipse or the Spring Tool Suite (_STS_).
- [Import Into Intellij Idea](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/import-into-intellij-idea.md): The following has been tested against IntelliJ IDEA 2016.2.2
- [Appendix](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/appendix.adoc): This part of the reference documentation covers topics that apply to multiple modules within the core Spring Framework.
- [Programmatic Creation of @AspectJ Proxies](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop/aspectj-programmatic.adoc): In addition to declaring aspects in your configuration by using either <aop:config> or <aop:aspectj-autoproxy>, it is also possible to programmatically create proxies that advise target objects.
- [Declaring Advice](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop/ataspectj/advice.adoc): Advice is associated with a pointcut expression and runs before, after, or around method executions matched by the pointcut.
- [Enabling @AspectJ Support](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop/ataspectj/aspectj-support.adoc): To use @AspectJ aspects in a Spring configuration, you need to enable Spring support for configuring Spring AOP based on @AspectJ aspects and auto-proxying beans based on whether or not they are advised by those aspects.
- [Declaring an Aspect](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop/ataspectj/at-aspectj.adoc): With @AspectJ support enabled, any bean defined in your application context with a class that is an @AspectJ aspect (has the @Aspect annotation) is automatically detected by Spring and used to configure Spring AOP.
- [An AOP Example](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop/ataspectj/example.adoc): Now that you have seen how all the constituent parts work, we can put them together to do something useful.
- [Aspect Instantiation Models](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop/ataspectj/instantiation-models.adoc): NOTE: This is an advanced topic.
- [Introductions](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop/ataspectj/introductions.adoc): Introductions (known as inter-type declarations in AspectJ) enable an aspect to declare that advised objects implement a given interface, and to provide an implementation of that interface on behalf of those objects.
- [Declaring a Pointcut](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop/ataspectj/pointcuts.adoc): Pointcuts determine join points of interest and thus enable us to control when advice runs.
- [@AspectJ support](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop/ataspectj.adoc): @AspectJ refers to a style of declaring aspects as regular Java classes annotated with annotations.
- [Choosing which AOP Declaration Style to Use](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop/choosing.adoc): Once you have decided that an aspect is the best approach for implementing a given requirement, how do you decide between using Spring AOP or AspectJ and between the Aspect language (code) style, the @AspectJ annotation style, or the Spring XML style?
- [AOP Concepts](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop/introduction-defn.adoc): Let us begin by defining some central AOP concepts and terminology.
- [AOP Proxies](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop/introduction-proxies.adoc): Spring AOP defaults to using standard JDK dynamic proxies for AOP proxies.
- [Spring AOP Capabilities and Goals](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop/introduction-spring-defn.adoc): Spring AOP is implemented in pure Java.
- [Mixing Aspect Types](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop/mixing-styles.adoc): It is perfectly possible to mix @AspectJ style aspects by using the auto-proxying support, schema-defined <aop:aspect> aspects, <aop:advisor> declared advisors, and even proxies and interceptors in other styles in the same configuration.
- [Proxying Mechanisms](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop/proxying.adoc): Spring AOP uses either JDK dynamic proxies or CGLIB to create the proxy for a given target object.
- [Further Resources](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop/resources.adoc): More information on AspectJ can be found on the {aspectj-site}[AspectJ website].
- [Schema-based AOP Support](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop/schema.adoc): If you prefer an XML-based format, Spring also offers support for defining aspects using the aop namespace tags.
- [Using AspectJ with Spring Applications](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop/using-aspectj.adoc): Everything we have covered so far in this chapter is pure Spring AOP.
- [Advice API in Spring](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop-api/advice.adoc): Now we can examine how Spring AOP handles advice.
- [Manipulating Advised Objects](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop-api/advised.adoc): However you create AOP proxies, you can manipulate them BY using the org.springframework.aop.framework.Advised interface.
- [The Advisor API in Spring](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop-api/advisor.adoc): In Spring, an Advisor is an aspect that contains only a single advice object associated with a pointcut expression.
- [Using the "auto-proxy" facility](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop-api/autoproxy.adoc): So far, we have considered explicit creation of AOP proxies by using a ProxyFactoryBean or similar factory bean.
- [Concise Proxy Definitions](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop-api/concise-proxy.adoc): Especially when defining transactional proxies, you may end up with many similar proxy definitions.
- [Defining New Advice Types](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop-api/extensibility.adoc): Spring AOP is designed to be extensible.
- [Using the `ProxyFactoryBean` to Create AOP Proxies](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop-api/pfb.adoc): If you use the Spring IoC container (an ApplicationContext or BeanFactory) for your business objects (and you should be!), you want to use one of Spring's AOP FactoryBean implementations.
- [Pointcut API in Spring](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop-api/pointcuts.adoc): This section describes how Spring handles the crucial pointcut concept.
- [Creating AOP Proxies Programmatically with the `ProxyFactory`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop-api/prog.adoc): It is easy to create AOP proxies programmatically with Spring.
- [Using `TargetSource` Implementations](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop-api/targetsource.adoc): Spring offers the concept of a TargetSource, expressed in the org.springframework.aop.TargetSource interface.
- [Aspect Oriented Programming with Spring](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop.adoc): Aspect-oriented Programming (AOP) complements Object-oriented Programming (OOP) by providing another way of thinking about program structure.
- [Ahead of Time Optimizations](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aot.adoc): This chapter covers Spring's Ahead of Time (AOT) optimizations.
- [Application Startup Steps](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/appendix/application-startup-steps.adoc): This part of the appendix lists the existing StartupSteps that the core container is instrumented with.
- [XML Schema Authoring](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/appendix/xml-custom.adoc): Since version 2.0, Spring has featured a mechanism for adding schema-based extensions to the basic Spring XML format for defining and configuring beans.
- [XML Schemas](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/appendix/xsd-schemas.adoc): This part of the appendix lists XML schemas related to the core container.
- [Appendix](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/appendix.adoc)
- [Fine-tuning Annotation-based Autowiring with `@Primary` or `@Fallback`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/annotation-config/autowired-primary.adoc): Because autowiring by type may lead to multiple candidates, it is often necessary to have more control over the selection process.
- [Fine-tuning Annotation-based Autowiring with Qualifiers](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/annotation-config/autowired-qualifiers.adoc): @Primary and @Fallback are effective ways to use autowiring by type with several instances when one primary (or non-fallback) candidate can be determined.
- [Using `@Autowired`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/annotation-config/autowired.adoc): JSR 330's @Inject annotation can be used in place of Spring's @Autowired annotation in the examples included in this section.
- [Using `CustomAutowireConfigurer`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/annotation-config/custom-autowire-configurer.adoc): {spring-framework-api}/beans/factory/annotation/CustomAutowireConfigurer.html[CustomAutowireConfigurer] is a BeanFactoryPostProcessor that lets you register your own custom qualifier annotation types, even if they are not annotated with Spring's @Qualifier annotation.
- [Using Generics as Autowiring Qualifiers](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/annotation-config/generics-as-qualifiers.adoc): In addition to the @Qualifier annotation, you can use Java generic types as an implicit form of qualification.
- [Using `@PostConstruct` and `@PreDestroy`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/annotation-config/postconstruct-and-predestroy-annotations.adoc): The CommonAnnotationBeanPostProcessor not only recognizes the @Resource annotation but also the JSR-250 lifecycle annotations: jakarta.annotation.PostConstruct and jakarta.annotation.PreDestroy.
- [Injection with `@Resource`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/annotation-config/resource.adoc): Spring also supports injection by using the JSR-250 @Resource annotation (jakarta.annotation.Resource) on fields or bean property setter methods.
- [Using `@Value`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/annotation-config/value-annotations.adoc): @Value is typically used to inject externalized properties:
- [Annotation-based Container Configuration](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/annotation-config.adoc): Spring provides comprehensive support for annotation-based configuration, operating on metadata in the component class itself by using annotations on the relevant class, method, or field declaration.
- [Container Overview](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/basics.adoc): The org.springframework.context.ApplicationContext interface represents the Spring IoC container and is responsible for instantiating, configuring, and assembling the beans.
- [The `BeanFactory` API](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/beanfactory.adoc): The BeanFactory API provides the underlying basis for Spring's IoC functionality.
- [Bean Definition Inheritance](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/child-bean-definitions.adoc): A bean definition can contain a lot of configuration information, including constructor arguments, property values, and container-specific information, such as the initialization method, a static factory method name, and so on.
- [Classpath Scanning and Managed Components](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/classpath-scanning.adoc): Most examples in this chapter use XML to specify the configuration metadata that produces each BeanDefinition within the Spring container.
- [Additional Capabilities of the `ApplicationContext`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/context-introduction.adoc): As discussed in the chapter introduction, the org.springframework.beans.factory package provides basic functionality for managing and manipulating beans, including in a programmatic way.
- [Registering a `LoadTimeWeaver`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/context-load-time-weaver.adoc): The LoadTimeWeaver is used by Spring to dynamically transform classes as they are loaded into the Java virtual machine (JVM).
- [Bean Overview](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/definition.adoc): A Spring IoC container manages one or more beans.
- [Autowiring Collaborators](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/dependencies/factory-autowire.adoc): The Spring container can autowire relationships between collaborating beans.
- [Dependency Injection](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/dependencies/factory-collaborators.adoc): Dependency injection (DI) is a process whereby objects define their dependencies (that is, the other objects with which they work) only through constructor arguments, arguments to a factory method, or properties that are set on the object instance after it is constructed or returned from a factory method.
- [Using `depends-on`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/dependencies/factory-dependson.adoc): If a bean is a dependency of another bean, that usually means that one bean is set as a property of another.
- [Lazy-initialized Beans](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/dependencies/factory-lazy-init.adoc): By default, ApplicationContext implementations eagerly create and configure all
- [Method Injection](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/dependencies/factory-method-injection.adoc): In most application scenarios, most beans in the container are
- [Dependencies and Configuration in Detail](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/dependencies/factory-properties-detailed.adoc): As mentioned in the previous section, you can define bean properties and constructor arguments as references to other managed beans (collaborators) or as values defined inline.
- [Dependencies](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/dependencies.adoc): A typical enterprise application does not consist of a single object (or bean in the Spring parlance).
- [Environment Abstraction](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/environment.adoc): The {spring-framework-api}/core/env/Environment.html[Environment] interface is an abstraction integrated in the container that models two key aspects of the application environment: profiles and properties.
- [Container Extension Points](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/factory-extension.adoc): Typically, an application developer does not need to subclass ApplicationContext implementation classes.
- [Customizing the Nature of a Bean](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/factory-nature.adoc): The Spring Framework provides a number of interfaces you can use to customize the nature of a bean.
- [Bean Scopes](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/factory-scopes.adoc): When you create a bean definition, you create a recipe for creating actual instances of the class defined by that bean definition.
- [Introduction to the Spring IoC Container and Beans](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/introduction.adoc): This chapter covers the Spring Framework implementation of the Inversion of Control (IoC) principle.
- [Basic Concepts: `@Bean` and `@Configuration`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/java/basic-concepts.adoc): The central artifacts in Spring's Java configuration support are @Configuration-annotated classes and @Bean-annotated methods.
- [Using the `@Bean` Annotation](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/java/bean-annotation.adoc): @Bean is a method-level annotation and a direct analog of the XML <bean/> element.
- [Composing Java-based Configurations](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/java/composing-configuration-classes.adoc): Spring's Java-based configuration feature lets you compose annotations, which can reduce the complexity of your configuration.
- [Using the `@Configuration` annotation](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/java/configuration-annotation.adoc): @Configuration is a class-level annotation indicating that an object is a source of bean definitions.
- [Instantiating the Spring Container by Using `AnnotationConfigApplicationContext`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/java/instantiating-container.adoc): The following sections document Spring's AnnotationConfigApplicationContext, introduced in Spring 3.0.
- [Programmatic Bean Registration](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/java/programmatic-bean-registration.adoc): As of Spring Framework 7, a first-class support for programmatic bean registration is provided via the {spring-framework-api}/beans/factory/BeanRegistrar.html[BeanRegistrar] interface that can be implemented to register beans programmatically in a flexible and efficient way.
- [Java-based Container Configuration](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/java.adoc): This section covers how to use annotations in your Java code to configure the Spring container.
- [Using JSR-330 Standard Annotations](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans/standard-annotations.adoc): Spring offers support for JSR-330 standard Dependency Injection annotations which are available in the jakarta.inject package.
- [The IoC Container](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/beans.adoc): This chapter covers Spring's Inversion of Control (IoC) container.
- [Data Buffers and Codecs](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/databuffer-codec.adoc): Java NIO provides ByteBuffer but many libraries build their own byte buffer API on top, especially for network operations where reusing buffers and/or using direct buffers is beneficial for performance.
- [Expressions in Bean Definitions](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/beandef.adoc): You can use SpEL expressions with configuration metadata for defining bean instances.
- [Evaluation](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/evaluation.adoc): This section introduces programmatic use of SpEL's interfaces and its expression language.
- [Classes Used in the Examples](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/example-classes.adoc): This section lists the classes used in the examples throughout this chapter.
- [Array Construction](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/language-ref/array-construction.adoc): You can build arrays by using the familiar Java syntax, optionally supplying an initializer to have the array populated at construction time.
- [Bean References](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/language-ref/bean-references.adoc): If the evaluation context has been configured with a bean resolver, you can look up beans from an expression by using the @ symbol as a prefix.
- [Collection Projection](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/language-ref/collection-projection.adoc): Projection lets a collection drive the evaluation of a sub-expression, and the result is a new collection.
- [Collection Selection](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/language-ref/collection-selection.adoc): Selection is a powerful expression language feature that lets you transform a source collection into another collection by selecting from its entries.
- [Constructors](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/language-ref/constructors.adoc): You can invoke constructors by using the new operator.
- [Functions](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/language-ref/functions.adoc): You can extend SpEL by registering user-defined functions that can be called within expressions by using the #functionName(...) syntax, and like with standard method invocations, varargs are also supported for function invocations.
- [Inline Lists](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/language-ref/inline-lists.adoc): You can directly express lists in an expression by using {} notation.
- [Inline Maps](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/language-ref/inline-maps.adoc): You can also directly express maps in an expression by using {key:value} notation.
- [Literal Expressions](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/language-ref/literal.adoc): SpEL supports the following types of literal expressions.
- [Methods](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/language-ref/methods.adoc): You can invoke methods by using the typical Java programming syntax.
- [The Elvis Operator](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/language-ref/operator-elvis.adoc): The Elvis operator (?:) is a shortening of the ternary operator syntax and is used in the Groovy language.
- [Safe Navigation Operator](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/language-ref/operator-safe-navigation.adoc): The safe navigation operator (?.) is used to avoid a NullPointerException and comes from the Groovy language.
- [Ternary Operator (If-Then-Else)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/language-ref/operator-ternary.adoc): You can use the ternary operator for performing if-then-else conditional logic inside the expression.
- [Operators](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/language-ref/operators.adoc): The Spring Expression Language supports the following kinds of operators:
- [Properties, Arrays, Lists, Maps, and Indexers](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/language-ref/properties-arrays.adoc): The Spring Expression Language provides support for navigating object graphs and indexing into various structures.
- [Expression Templating](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/language-ref/templating.adoc): Expression templates allow mixing literal text with one or more evaluation blocks.
- [Types](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/language-ref/types.adoc): You can use the special T operator to specify an instance of java.lang.Class (the type).
- [Varargs Invocations](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/language-ref/varargs.adoc): The Spring Expression Language supports varargs invocations for constructors,
- [Variables](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/language-ref/variables.adoc): You can reference variables in an expression by using the #variableName syntax.
- [Language Reference](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions/language-ref.adoc): Spring Expression Language (SpEL) expressions are composed of a sequence of tokens such as literals, operators, method invocations, and so forth.
- [Spring Expression Language (SpEL)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/expressions.adoc): The Spring Expression Language ("SpEL" for short) is a powerful expression language that supports querying and manipulating an object graph at runtime.
- [Null-safety](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/null-safety.adoc): Although Java does not let you express nullness markers with its type system yet, the Spring Framework codebase is annotated with JSpecify annotations to declare the nullability of its APIs, fields, and related type usages.
- [Resilience Features](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/resilience.adoc): As of 7.0, the core Spring Framework includes common resilience features, in particular <<resilience-annotations-retryable>> and <<resilience-annotations-concurrencylimit>> annotations for method invocations as well as <<resilience-programmatic-retry, programmatic retry support>>.
- [Resources](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/resources.adoc): This chapter covers how Spring handles resources and how you can work with resources in Spring.
- [Java Bean Validation](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/validation/beanvalidation.adoc): The Spring Framework provides support for the {bean-validation-site}[Java Bean Validation] API.
- [Spring Type Conversion](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/validation/convert.adoc): The core.convert package provides a general type conversion system.

- [Spring JUnit Jupiter Testing Annotations](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-junit-jupiter.adoc): The following annotations are supported when used in conjunction with the
- [Spring JUnit 4 Testing Annotations](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-junit4.adoc): JUnit 4 support is deprecated since Spring Framework 7.0 in favor of the
- [Meta-Annotation Support for Testing](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-meta.adoc): You can use most test-related annotations as
- [`@ActiveProfiles`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring/annotation-activeprofiles.adoc): @ActiveProfiles is an annotation that can be applied to a test class to declare which bean definition profiles should be active when loading an ApplicationContext for an integration test.
- [`@AfterTransaction`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring/annotation-aftertransaction.adoc): @AfterTransaction indicates that the annotated void method should be run after a transaction is ended, for test methods that have been configured to run within a transaction by using Spring's @Transactional annotation.
- [`@BeforeTransaction`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring/annotation-beforetransaction.adoc): @BeforeTransaction indicates that the annotated void method should be run before a transaction is started, for test methods that have been configured to run within a transaction by using Spring's @Transactional annotation.
- [`@BootstrapWith`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring/annotation-bootstrapwith.adoc): @BootstrapWith is an annotation that can be applied to a test class to configure how the Spring TestContext Framework is bootstrapped.
- [`@Commit`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring/annotation-commit.adoc): @Commit indicates that the transaction for a transactional test method should be committed after the test method has completed.
- [`@ContextConfiguration`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring/annotation-contextconfiguration.adoc): @ContextConfiguration is an annotation that can be applied to a test class to configure metadata that is used to determine how to load and configure an ApplicationContext for integration tests.
- [`@ContextCustomizerFactories`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring/annotation-contextcustomizerfactories.adoc): @ContextCustomizerFactories is an annotation that can be applied to a test class to register ContextCustomizerFactory implementations for the particular test class, its subclasses, and its nested classes.
- [`@ContextHierarchy`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring/annotation-contexthierarchy.adoc): @ContextHierarchy is an annotation that can be applied to a test class to define a hierarchy of ApplicationContext instances for integration tests.
- [`@DirtiesContext`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring/annotation-dirtiescontext.adoc): @DirtiesContext indicates that the underlying Spring ApplicationContext has been dirtied during the execution of a test (that is, the test modified or corrupted it in some manner -- for example, by changing the state of a singleton bean) and should be closed.
- [`@DisabledInAotMode`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring/annotation-disabledinaotmode.adoc): @DisabledInAotMode signals that the annotated test class is disabled in Spring AOT (ahead-of-time) mode, which means that the ApplicationContext for the test class will not be processed for AOT optimizations at build time.
- [`@DynamicPropertySource`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring/annotation-dynamicpropertysource.adoc): @DynamicPropertySource is an annotation that can be applied to methods in integration test classes that need to register dynamic properties to be added to the set of PropertySources in the Environment for an ApplicationContext loaded for an integration test.
- [`@MockitoBean` and `@MockitoSpyBean`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring/annotation-mockitobean.adoc): {spring-framework-api}/test/context/bean/override/mockito/MockitoBean.html[@MockitoBean] and {spring-framework-api}/test/context/bean/override/mockito/MockitoSpyBean.html[@MockitoSpyBean] can be used in test classes to override a bean in the test's ApplicationContext with a Mockito mock or spy, respectively.
- [`@RecordApplicationEvents`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring/annotation-recordapplicationevents.adoc): @RecordApplicationEvents is an annotation that can be applied to a test class to instruct the Spring TestContext Framework to record all application events that are published in the ApplicationContext during the execution of a single test.
- [`@Rollback`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring/annotation-rollback.adoc): @Rollback indicates whether the transaction for a transactional test method should be rolled back after the test method has completed.
- [`@Sql`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring/annotation-sql.adoc): @Sql is used to annotate a test class or test method to configure SQL scripts to be run against a given database during integration tests.
- [`@SqlConfig`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring/annotation-sqlconfig.adoc): @SqlConfig defines metadata that is used to determine how to parse and run SQL scripts configured with the @Sql annotation.
- [`@SqlGroup`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring/annotation-sqlgroup.adoc): @SqlGroup is a container annotation that aggregates several @Sql annotations.
- [`@SqlMergeMode`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring/annotation-sqlmergemode.adoc): @SqlMergeMode is used to annotate a test class or test method to configure whether method-level @Sql declarations are merged with class-level @Sql declarations.
- [`@TestBean`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring/annotation-testbean.adoc): {spring-framework-api}/test/context/bean/override/convention/TestBean.html[@TestBean] is used on a non-static field in a test class to override a specific bean in the test's ApplicationContext with an instance provided by a factory method.
- [`@TestExecutionListeners`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring/annotation-testexecutionlisteners.adoc): @TestExecutionListeners is used to register listeners for the annotated test class, its subclasses, and its nested classes.
- [`@TestPropertySource`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring/annotation-testpropertysource.adoc): @TestPropertySource is an annotation that can be applied to a test class to configure the locations of properties files and inlined properties to be added to the set of PropertySources in the Environment for an ApplicationContext loaded for an integration test.
- [`@WebAppConfiguration`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring/annotation-webappconfiguration.adoc): @WebAppConfiguration is an annotation that can be applied to a test class to declare that the ApplicationContext loaded for an integration test should be a WebApplicationContext.
- [Spring Testing Annotations](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-spring.adoc): The Spring Framework provides the following set of Spring-specific annotations that you can use in your unit and integration tests in conjunction with the TestContext framework.
- [Standard Annotation Support](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/testing/annotations/integration-standard.adoc): The following annotations are supported with standard semantics for all configurations of the Spring TestContext Framework.

- [RSS and Atom](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/webmvc-view/mvc-feeds.adoc): WARNING: As of Spring Framework 7.0, view classes in the org.springframework.web.servlet.view.feed package are deprecated.
- [HTML Fragments](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/webmvc-view/mvc-fragments.adoc): HTMX and Hotwire Turbo emphasize an HTML-over-the-wire approach where clients receive server updates in HTML rather than in JSON.
- [FreeMarker](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/webmvc-view/mvc-freemarker.adoc): Apache FreeMarker is a template engine for generating any kind of text output from HTML to email and others.
- [Groovy Markup](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/webmvc-view/mvc-groovymarkup.adoc): The Groovy Markup Template Engine is primarily aimed at generating XML-like markup (XML, XHTML, HTML5, and others), but you can use it to generate any text-based content.
- [Jackson](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/webmvc-view/mvc-jackson.adoc): Spring offers support for the Jackson JSON library.
- [JSP and JSTL](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/webmvc-view/mvc-jsp.adoc): The Spring Framework has a built-in integration for using Spring MVC with JSP and JSTL.
- [Script Views](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/webmvc-view/mvc-script.adoc): The Spring Framework has a built-in integration for using Spring MVC with any templating library that can run on top of the {JSR}223[JSR-223] Java scripting engine.
- [Thymeleaf](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/webmvc-view/mvc-thymeleaf.adoc): Thymeleaf is a modern server-side Java template engine that emphasizes natural HTML templates that can be previewed in a browser by double-clicking, which is very helpful for independent work on UI templates (for example, by a designer) without the need for a running server.
- [XML Marshalling](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/webmvc-view/mvc-xml-marshalling.adoc): The MarshallingView uses an XML Marshaller (defined in the org.springframework.oxm package) to render the response content as XML.
- [XSLT Views](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/webmvc-view/mvc-xslt.adoc): XSLT is a transformation language for XML and is popular as a view technology within web applications.
- [View Technologies](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/webmvc-view.adoc): The rendering of views in Spring MVC is pluggable.
- [Spring Web MVC](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/webmvc.adoc): Spring Web MVC is the original web framework built on the Servlet API and has been included in the Spring Framework from the very beginning.
- [SockJS Fallback](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/fallback.adoc): Over the public Internet, restrictive proxies outside your control may preclude WebSocket interactions, either because they are not configured to pass on the Upgrade header or because they close long-lived connections that appear to be idle.
- [WebSocket API](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/server.adoc): The Spring Framework provides a WebSocket API that you can use to write client- and server-side applications that handle WebSocket messages.
- [Events](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/application-context-events.adoc): Several ApplicationContext events are published and can be received by implementing Spring's ApplicationListener interface:
- [Token Authentication](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/authentication-token-based.adoc): {spring-github-org}/spring-security-oauth[Spring Security OAuth] provides support for token based security, including JSON Web Token (JWT).
- [Authentication](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/authentication.adoc): Every STOMP over WebSocket messaging session begins with an HTTP request.
- [Authorization](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/authorization.adoc): Spring Security provides {docs-spring-security}/servlet/integrations/websocket.html#websocket-authorization[WebSocket sub-protocol authorization] that uses a ChannelInterceptor to authorize messages based on the user header in them.
- [Benefits](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/benefits.adoc): Using STOMP as a sub-protocol lets the Spring Framework and Spring Security provide a richer programming model versus using raw WebSockets.
- [STOMP Client](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/client.adoc): Spring provides a STOMP over WebSocket client and a STOMP over TCP client.
- [Performance](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/configuration-performance.adoc): There is no silver bullet when it comes to performance.
- [Dots as Separators](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/destination-separator.adoc): When messages are routed to @MessageMapping methods, they are matched with AntPathMatcher.
- [Enable STOMP](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/enable.adoc): STOMP over WebSocket support is available in the spring-messaging and spring-websocket modules.
- [Annotated Controllers](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/handle-annotations.adoc): Applications can use annotated @Controller classes to handle messages from clients.
- [Connecting to a Broker](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/handle-broker-relay-configure.adoc): A STOMP broker relay maintains a single "system" TCP connection to the broker.
- [External Broker](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/handle-broker-relay.adoc): The simple broker is great for getting started but supports only a subset of STOMP commands (it does not support acks, receipts, and some other features), relies on a simple message-sending loop, and is not suitable for clustering.
- [Sending Messages](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/handle-send.adoc): What if you want to send messages to connected clients from any part of the application?
- [Simple Broker](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/handle-simple-broker.adoc): The built-in simple message broker handles subscription requests from clients, stores them in memory, and broadcasts messages to connected clients that have matching destinations.
- [Interception](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/interceptors.adoc): of a STOMP connection but not for every client message.
- [Flow of Messages](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/message-flow.adoc): Once a STOMP endpoint is exposed, the Spring application becomes a STOMP broker for connected clients.
- [Order of Messages](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/ordered-messages.adoc): Messages from the broker are published to the clientOutboundChannel, from where they are written to WebSocket sessions.
- [Overview](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/overview.adoc): STOMP (Simple Text Oriented Messaging Protocol) was originally created for scripting languages (such as Ruby, Python, and Perl) to connect to enterprise message brokers.
- [WebSocket Scope](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/scope.adoc): Each WebSocket session has a map of attributes.
- [WebSocket Transport](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/server-config.adoc): This section explains how to configure the underlying WebSocket server transport.
- [Monitoring](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/stats.adoc): When you use @EnableWebSocketMessageBroker or <websocket:message-broker>, key infrastructure components automatically gather statistics and counters that provide important insight into the internal state of the application.
- [Testing](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/testing.adoc): There are two main approaches to testing applications when you use Spring's STOMP-over-WebSocket support.
- [User Destinations](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp/user-destination.adoc): An application can send messages that target a specific user, and Spring's STOMP support recognizes destinations prefixed with /user/ for this purpose.
- [STOMP](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket/stomp.adoc): The WebSocket protocol defines two types of messages (text and binary), but their content is undefined.
- [WebSockets](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/websocket.adoc): This part of the reference documentation covers support for Servlet stack, WebSocket messaging that includes raw WebSocket interactions, WebSocket emulation through SockJS, and publish-subscribe messaging through STOMP as a sub-protocol over WebSocket.
- [Web on Reactive Stack](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web-reactive.adoc): This part of the documentation covers support for reactive-stack web applications built on a {reactive-streams-site}/[Reactive Streams] API to run on non-blocking servers, such as Netty and Servlet containers.
- [Web on Servlet Stack](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web.adoc): This part of the documentation covers support for Servlet-stack web applications built on the Servlet API and deployed to Servlet containers.
- [Forwarded Headers](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/partials/web/forwarded-headers.adoc): As a request goes through proxies such as load balancers the host, port, and scheme may change, and that makes it a challenge to create links that point to the correct host, port, and scheme from a client perspective.
- [Uri Patterns](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/partials/web/uri-patterns.adoc): +"/projects/*/versions"+ matches +"/projects/spring/versions"+ but does not match +"/projects/spring/boot/versions"+.
- [Web Data Binding Model Design](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/partials/web/web-data-binding-model-design.adoc): Data binding involves binding untrusted input onto application objects.
- [UriComponents](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/partials/web/web-uris.adoc): UriComponentsBuilder helps to build URIs from URI templates with variables, as the following example shows:
- [Introduction to WebSocket](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/partials/web/websocket-intro.adoc): The WebSocket protocol, {rfc-site}/rfc6455[RFC 6455], provides a standardized way to establish a full-duplex, two-way communication channel between client and server over a single TCP connection.

## API Reference

- [Spring AOP APIs](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/core/aop-api.adoc): The previous chapter described the Spring's support for AOP with @AspectJ and schema-based aspect definitions.

- [Reporting a Vulnerability](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/SECURITY.md): Please, open a draft security advisory if you need to disclose and discuss a security issue in private with the Spring Framework team.
- [Web Security](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/main/framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/web/webmvc/mvc-security.adoc): The {spring-site-projects}/spring-security[Spring Security] project provides support for protecting web applications from malicious exploits.
